audit.why: Pantheon 1 / Skill 2 / Tryndamere 3-4 / Pantheon 6 / Tryndamere at both item stages, agreed across both layers and consistent with 52.99% over 953 games and with the prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole level-6 discussion turns on Undying Rage and never gives its cooldown.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80s. 'Don't dump your combo expecting a kill at full fury' becomes actionable when the player knows a baited ult buys them two full minutes. Mocking Shout is a flat 14s and Spinning Slash 12s at rank 1 (650 range).
audit.corrected: Undying Rage's 120s written into mid, whys[4], spikes[3], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is never mentioned anywhere in the matchup — not in either layer.
audit.why: Riot: 'Tryndamere lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' Two things Pantheon needs: his W cuts the attack damage half of your trade, and it only slows you if you turn to run. Retreating while facing him is free; turning your back is what gets you killed. This is the most useful unstated fact in the pairing.
audit.corrected: Written into early, wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Bloodlust is never named, and the page implies a low Tryndamere is a weak one.
audit.why: Riot: Bloodlust increases his Attack Damage as he is more wounded, and casting it consumes Fury to heal. Both halves matter and neither was stated — a nearly dead Tryndamere hits harder, and the healing is what makes Grievous Wounds a real item here. _missing-interactions flags needs-antiheal for this pairing.
audit.corrected: Named in early, whys[3], late and wants.foe[2]; Grievous Wounds added to whys[5], mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'pop E (Aegis Assault) to block his autos from that direction' is right but vague; elsewhere it is just 'E blocks'.
audit.why: Aegis Assault is invulnerable to damage from the front only — worth saying plainly next to a champion whose entire output is basic attacks.
audit.corrected: Stated as facing the shield at his autos in early, whys[2] and spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright'.
audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will; there is no passive shield.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are all yours. Tryndamere is a weak early-laner with no fury and no crit, so your point-and-click W stun plus an empowered-Q burst chunks him for free before he can spin back. When he spins in to trade, pop E (Aegis Assault) to block his autos from that direction and his damage just evaporates. Don't waste your all-in when he's already low on fury — he can't punish you, so just keep poking and force a clean level-3 trade.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are all yours. Tryndamere is a weak early laner with no Fury and no crit, so your point-and-click Shield Vault plus an empowered Comet Spear chunks him for free before he spins back. Face Aegis Assault at his autos when he spins in and the damage evaporates. Two things the lane runs on: Bloodlust heals him by spending Fury, and Mocking Shout cuts your attack damage and slows you only if your back is turned — so retreat facing him.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 you stay ahead: empowered-Q poke and E blocks let you control the wave and chip him every time he steps up to farm. At 6 your Grand Starfall is for roaming, not the 1v1 — use it to leap onto a sidelane or the enemy jungler and convert your lead, because the longer this lane sits 1v1 the closer Trynd gets to his crit spike. Just respect that once he hits Undying Rage he can ignore your burst, so don't dump your whole combo expecting a kill at full fury.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 you stay ahead: empowered-Q poke and Aegis Assault let you control the wave and chip him every time he steps up to farm. At 6 Grand Starfall is for roaming, not the 1v1 — leap onto a sidelane or the enemy jungler, because the longer this lane sits 1v1 the closer Trynd gets to his crit spike. Respect Undying Rage: it is 120 seconds at rank 1, so bait it rather than dumping your combo into it, and buy Grievous Wounds for Bloodlust.

edits.before: By two items this flips hard. Tryndamere's R lets him survive your entire combo at 1 HP for five seconds, and once he has crit items his spin out-DPSes your plateaued damage and shreds your squishy frame. You cannot kill him through Undying Rage and he'll just spin-kite you to death. Your only path is the lead you already built — end the game on the back of your early snowball and roams before his crit comes fully online.
edits.after: By two items this flips hard. Undying Rage lets him survive your entire combo, and once he has crit items his spin out-DPSes your plateaued damage. Bloodlust also hands him more attack damage the lower he drops, so a nearly dead Tryndamere is the dangerous one and Grievous Wounds stops being optional. You cannot kill him through the ult and he will spin-kite you down. End on your early snowball before his crit comes fully online.

edits.before: Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright. Identify how Tryndamere contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Mortal Will empowers your next cast and Comet Spear beats an empty Fury bar — level 1 is yours before crit chance exists.

edits.before: Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright. Respect Tryndamere's Undying Rage completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Mortal Will plus Comet Spear wins level 1 outright. Respect Undying Rage's 120s at rank 1 — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. Burst him before he R’s. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1 — he cannot die through it, so bait it and take the two minutes after. - Mocking Shout: 14s, cuts your AD and slows you if your back is turned. - Spinning Slash: 12s at 650.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. Burst him before he R’s. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: He cannot die through it, and it is 120s at rank 1. Bait it, then burst.

edits.before: Track Tryndamere's Undying Rage: Unkillable 5s. Burst him before he R’s. When it is down — W-Q burst him.
edits.after: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 — bait it out. Mocking Shout cuts your AD and slows a turned back.

notes: The biggest gap here is an omission rather than an error: Mocking Shout appears nowhere in either layer. It decreases the attack damage of nearby champions and slows only enemies whose backs are turned. For Pantheon that is two concrete instructions — his W eats the auto-attack half of your trade, and you should walk away facing him rather than turning to run. Bloodlust was also unnamed, and the page's framing implies a low-health Tryndamere is a weak one when Riot's text says the opposite: his attack damage rises as he is more wounded, and casting Bloodlust converts Fury into healing. That is also why Grievous Wounds matters, which _missing-interactions flags and the page never mentioned. Added Undying Rage's 120-second rank-1 cooldown so 'bait his ult' has a payoff the player can count. NOT ASSERTED: the existing text states Undying Rage lasts five seconds. Riot's description gives no duration and I could not verify it, so I neither repeated nor removed the number where it already stands — my own lines avoid it.
